title: Choose the Axiom visual world
question: Choose the design system family that should lead all three image-first storefronts.

options.label: Three Material Rooms
options.lineage: specialist retail interiors, editorial lookbooks, and material libraries
options.thesis: One Axiom threshold opens into three unmistakable physical worlds built around each catalog's real imagery.
options.viewport: Each storefront opens on a near-full-screen photograph with a compact glass navigation ribbon and typography composed into the image; the next product rail visibly enters at the fold.
options.risk: The family connection disappears if the shared Axiom wordmark and interaction rhythm are not disciplined.

raised.raise: Product measurements and prices receive an exact, stable data rhythm rather than decorative technical type.
Each room gets one atmospheric transition and a reduced-motion still state, while photography remains the subject.
Category navigation becomes a truthful visual contents map anchored in real catalog images.
Foreground, image, and copy settle in deliberate layers instead of generic card stacks.

options.label: Axiom Field Editions
options.lineage: independent culture magazines, specimen monographs, and collector catalogues
options.thesis: Each storefront is a different editorial edition: crop-led, typographically fearless, and designed to make products feel collected rather than listed.
options.viewport: An asymmetrical cover composition pairs one decisive product photograph with a large edition title, a narrow glass nav, and a horizontal visual index crossing the fold.
options.risk: Editorial commerce is familiar and can feel like a magazine template if product controls are not integrated boldly.

options.label: Living Material Portal
options.lineage: experiential studios and full-bleed shader portals
options.thesis: Catalog photography floats inside slow living color fields that react to movement and dissolve between storefront rooms.
options.viewport: One product world fills the screen behind thin floating navigation; pointer movement subtly refracts the image and route changes dissolve the color field.
options.case: It wins memorability and audience intrigue but holds less product clarity than the assigned image-led rooms.
options.risk: Motion and rendering cost can compete with shopping speed on lower-powered phones.

options.label: Compartment Catalogue
options.lineage: station ekiben wrappers and mapped compartment boxes
options.thesis: The catalog becomes a visual contents map with every category occupying a named photographic compartment.
options.viewport: A photographic compartment map replaces the conventional hero and opens directly into categories.
options.case: The map clarifies breadth, but the literal boxed-meal structure does not identify naturally with all three audiences.
options.kept: Category imagery must function as navigation, not decoration.
options.risk: The compartment metaphor can overpower premium product presentation.

canonCard.label: Polished category standard
canonCard.thesis: A premium ecommerce grid with strong photography, familiar navigation, and restrained storefront color themes.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional split hero, category cards, and product grid executed at a high craft level.
canonCard.risk: Easy to use, but the three storefronts remain structurally interchangeable.
